chapters.title: Chapter 2: Who Needs to Pay Advance Tax

lessons.title: The 10,000 Rupee Rule: How to Tell If Advance Tax Applies to You

body.text: Advance tax does not depend on how much you earn. It depends on how much tax is still unpaid after TDS and TCS. If your estimated tax for the year, net of those credits, is ₹10,000 or more, you must pay advance tax. Below that, you can settle up when you file.

children.text: A senior executive earning ₹50 lakh a year can owe no advance tax at all, because TDS on salary covers everything. A first-year freelancer earning ₹14 lakh can owe nearly ₹94,000 of it. The difference is not income. It is the gap between the tax you owe and the tax someone else has already deposited for you.

markDefs.definition: A reduction in tax for lower incomes. Under the new regime, section 156 (old 87A) gives a rebate of up to ₹60,000, making slab income up to ₹12 lakh effectively tax-free.
Tax collected at source. The seller or remitter collects tax from you at the time of certain purchases or payments, such as large foreign remittances, and credits it to your PAN.

TCS collected from you and credited to your PAN
The rebate on slab income under section 156

body.title: Show me the math: Isha, Dev and Meenal

children.text: Isha: slab tax on ₹11,00,000 is ₹20,000 (5% on ₹4 to 8 lakh) plus ₹30,000 (10% on ₹8 to 11 lakh), which is ₹50,000. Her slab income is within ₹12 lakh, so the rebate of up to ₹60,000 wipes it out. Tax: nil.

Dev: slab tax on ₹14,00,000 is ₹20,000 plus ₹40,000 plus ₹30,000 (15% on ₹12 to 14 lakh), which is ₹90,000. His income is above ₹12 lakh, so no rebate. Marginal relief does not help either, because ₹90,000 is less than the ₹2,00,000 by which he crosses ₹12 lakh. With 4% cess, tax is ₹93,600, and none of it is covered by TDS.

Meenal: salary of ₹9,00,000 less the ₹75,000 standard deduction is ₹8,25,000. Slab tax is ₹22,500, fully rebated, so her employer deducts no TDS. Her short-term gain of ₹1,50,000 on listed shares is taxed at 20%, which is ₹30,000. The rebate cannot be used against that tax, even though her slab income is under ₹12 lakh. With cess, ₹31,200 is due, all of it uncovered.

body.title: Quick Check: The Rebate Trap
body.question: Meenal's total income, including her short-term gain, is under ₹12 lakh. Her friend says, "Income under ₹12 lakh is tax-free in the new regime, so you have nothing to pay." Why is the friend wrong?
options: Because the ₹12 lakh limit applies to gross salary before the standard deduction
Because the rebate only covers tax on slab income, not the 20% tax on short-term gains from listed shares
Because freelancers and investors are not eligible for the rebate at all
The friend is right: Meenal owes nothing
body.explanation: The section 156 rebate (old 87A) can be set off only against tax on income taxed at slab rates. Tax on short-term gains under the special 20% rate, and on long-term gains from shares and equity funds, stays payable. This is one of the most common reasons first-time investors are surprised by advance tax.

body.title: Try It: Farah's FD Gap
body.prompt: Farah's salary is taxed at the 30% slab and her employer's TDS covers it fully. She also earns ₹60,000 of FD interest, on which her bank deducts TDS at 10%. Including 4% cess, how much tax is still due on the interest after TDS? Answer in rupees.
body.explanation: Tax on the interest is 30% of ₹60,000, which is ₹18,000, plus 4% cess, giving ₹18,720. The bank deducted ₹6,000. That leaves ₹12,720, which is above ₹10,000, so Farah must pay advance tax even though her only non-salary income is a bank FD.

children.text: Where the Line Falls for a Freelancer

For someone with no TDS at all, the new regime creates a sharp edge. Up to ₹12 lakh of slab income, the rebate means no tax and no advance tax. Just above it, marginal relief caps your tax at the amount by which you cross ₹12 lakh, and that quickly exceeds ₹10,000.

body.title: Tax including cess for a freelancer with no TDS, new regime, tax year 2026-27

body.text: At ₹12.5 lakh, tax before marginal relief would be ₹67,500. Marginal relief caps it at ₹50,000, the amount by which income exceeds ₹12 lakh, and cess takes it to ₹52,000. Marginal relief stops mattering at roughly ₹12.75 lakh. So a freelancer can go from zero advance tax to more than ₹50,000 of it with one extra client.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: What Is Being Tested
body.textWithBlank: The ₹10,000 advance tax threshold is applied to your estimated ___ for the year after subtracting TDS and TCS, not to your income.
body.explanation: Section 404 looks at tax, not income. A ₹50 lakh salary with full TDS can mean zero advance tax, while a ₹14 lakh freelance income with no TDS can mean more than ₹90,000 of it.

body.title: Scenario: Tanvi Switches Jobs
body.scenario: Tanvi, 29, works in marketing in Gurugram. From April to September 2026 she earns ₹9 lakh at her first employer. She joins a new company in October and earns ₹12 lakh there from October 2026 to March 2027. She does not tell her new employer about her earlier salary. When each employer settles its TDS on the salary it actually paid, each one applies the standard deduction and the rebate as if that salary were her only income, and the TDS comes to nil at both.
body.prompt: Is Tanvi liable for advance tax for tax year 2026-27? How much tax is at stake, and what is the simplest way to fix it?
body.modelAnswer: Yes. Her real salary for the year is ₹21 lakh. After one standard deduction of ₹75,000, her taxable income is ₹20,25,000. Slab tax is ₹2,06,250 (₹20,000 plus ₹40,000 plus ₹60,000 plus ₹80,000 plus 25% of ₹25,000), and with 4% cess it is ₹2,14,500. No rebate applies because her income is above ₹12 lakh. With nil TDS, all ₹2,14,500 is uncovered, far above ₹10,000. The simplest fix is to declare her previous salary and TDS to the new employer as soon as she joins, using the prescribed declaration for salary from a previous employer. The new employer then deducts the shortfall from her remaining payslips, and TDS actually deducted counts against her advance tax liability. Whatever cannot be covered that way she should pay as advance tax by the remaining due dates. Chapter 3 covers how to handle a mid-year change like this, and Chapter 4 the interest if she does nothing until she files.

body.title: Your ₹10,000 Check for Tax Year 2026-27
steps: List every income you expect this tax year, including salary, rent, FD and savings interest, dividends, capital gains and freelance or business income
Mark which of these have TDS or TCS, and check AIS on the e-filing portal to confirm what has actually been reported so far
Estimate tax on the full picture using the regime you will choose, applying the rebate only to slab income
Subtract only the TDS and TCS that has actually been, or will definitely be, deducted
If the balance is ₹10,000 or more, note the next instalment date and the cumulative percentage due by then
Repeat the check whenever you switch jobs, book a large gain or win a significant new client

cards.definition: Makes advance tax payable only when estimated tax for the year, after TDS and TCS, is ₹10,000 or more.
Explains how to compute advance tax: estimate income, apply rates, reduce rebate, relief, TDS and TCS.
Up to ₹60,000 off tax on slab income under the new regime when slab income is ₹12 lakh or less. Not available against special-rate capital gains tax.
Just above ₹12 lakh, caps tax before cess at the amount by which income exceeds ₹12 lakh.
Tax collected at source by a seller or remitter, credited to your PAN and deducted when computing advance tax.
If a payer fails to deduct TDS, you cannot subtract that missing TDS when working out advance tax.

points: Advance tax applies when estimated tax for the tax year, after TDS and TCS, is ₹10,000 or more
The test is on tax still due, not on income: high earners with full TDS may owe nothing, while modest freelancers may owe a lot
Apply the ₹60,000 rebate only to slab income; tax on short-term and long-term gains from shares stays payable
Only TDS actually deducted counts; TDS a client should have deducted but did not cannot reduce your liability
Freelancers with no TDS cross the line almost immediately once slab income exceeds ₹12 lakh
Rerun the check after a job switch, a large capital gain or a new client
